A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Optimal kernel regression bounds under energy-bounded noise. All 31 pages in each version, including figures, equations, Table 1, and Technical Appendices A–D, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original numerical comparisons of uncertainty-region areas and safe-control success rates and computation times in Section 4.3, Figures 2–3. Appendix D documents the control experiment.

after.justification: v3 retains the original numerical experiments and their results in Section 4.3, Figures 2–3, with implementation details in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The RKHS-constrained formulation, relaxed bound, scalar optimization over the noise parameter, and special-case solutions remain unchanged. Adding the test-point argument in Equation (8) clarifies existing notation without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic kernel-regression setting on [0,4] and scalar nonlinear safe-control task on [-2,2] in Section 4.3. No dataset, domain, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains the optimal and fixed-noise-parameter bounded-energy bounds and the Abbasi-Yadkori (2013) probabilistic comparator. Figure 3 retains full-data bounded-energy, 10-nearest-neighbor bounded-energy, and full-data probabilistic comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix D preserve the kernels, noise distribution and magnitude, training-data sweep, 500-point control evaluation grid, evaluation metrics, and optimization settings.

E4.justification: The noise-parameter illustration, sample-size comparisons, and safe-control case study—including the full-data versus 10-nearest-neighbor analysis—are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report 1,000 random-function runs for Figure 2 and 20 repetitions for the safe-control experiment. Figures 2–3 retain the same 5th/95th-percentile shading and statistical reporting practices.

E6.justification: Figures 1–3 and their accompanying findings are unchanged, including the low-data advantage of energy-based bounds and the safe-control success/runtime tradeoff. No plotted results, numerical result entries, or rankings change.

T1.justification: The assumptions, mathematical results, and proofs in Appendices A–C are substantively unchanged. Section 3.1 corrects the duplicated reference '(2c), (2c)' to '(2c), (2d)'. Equation (8) adds the mean's test-point argument already present in Equation (5a) and Appendix B; neither edit changes mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution paragraph, and conclusion retain the same claims about exact non-asymptotic bounds, handling correlated and biased noise, recovering known special cases, and applicability to safe control.

C2.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 retain the interpretations of deterministic versus probabilistic bounds, data-subsetting tradeoffs, and limitations concerning kernel misspecification and known RKHS-norm bounds. The reflowed discussion introduces no substantive qualification.

D1.justification: Appendix D and Table 1 retain the controller parameters, slack feasibility threshold, CasADi/IPOPT implementation, and Intel i9-7940X hardware. The code-access text and embedded code-link targets are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Section 4.2 corrects 'Corrolary' to 'Corollary' for the same Kanagawa et al. (2025) result, without changing the citation or its interpretation.

P1.justification: Limited editorial corrections change 'data-points' to 'data points', fix 'Corrolary', repair the constraint reference, and make Equation (8)'s argument explicit. The version/date stamp is updated; section organization and narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The abstract and a paragraph in Section 4.3 have small line-wrap and spacing changes, and Equation (8) widens to accommodate its argument. Figures 1–3, Table 1, captions, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves editorial precision by correcting the constraint reference in Section 3.1 and making Equation (8) consistent with the explicit notation in Equation (5a) and Appendix B. These fixes reduce small reading ambiguities while leaving the theoretical support, experimental evidence, and reproducibility information unchanged.
